Today there is a growing awareness that mental well-being needs to be given as much attention as physical health. For too long, we have measured a person's health only by the body, ignoring the mind that quietly suffers behind a healthy-looking face. Yet a troubled mind can be just as disabling as a broken leg, which is why the two deserve equal care.
My own experience convinces me of this. During my sophomore year, a close friend kept a perfect exercise routine but slid into deep anxiety before exams. He looked strong, so no one noticed until his grades and sleep collapsed. Only after he sought counseling did he truly recover. His story shows that neglecting the mind can undo all the benefits of a fit body.
Therefore, we should treat mental and physical health as two wheels of the same cart. Schools and workplaces ought to offer counseling as readily as gyms, and each of us should learn to talk about our feelings without shame. When the mind is cared for as much as the body, a person can be genuinely, fully healthy.

lines.en: M: Hi, Lily, how's the new apartment?
lines.zh: M: 嗨，莉莉，新公寓怎么样？

lines.en: W: It's okay.
lines.zh: W: 还行吧。

lines.en: M: What? How can it be just okay when last week you were thrilled about the place and kept posting photos of it online?
lines.zh: M: 什么？上周你还对这个地方兴奋不已，还不停地把照片发到网上，怎么现在只能说还行？

lines.en: W: Well, last week when I moved in, the apartment seemed cozy, just the right size for one person. But now it just seems tiny, shabby and solitary.
lines.zh: W: 嗯，我上周搬进去的时候，觉得公寓很温馨，对一个人来说大小正合适。但现在我只觉得它又小又破旧，还很孤单。

lines.en: M: Ah, that's the problem. You miss your roommates from university, don't you?
lines.zh: M: 啊，问题就在这儿。你想念大学时的室友了，对吧？

lines.en: W: I'm going to sound like an idiot, because I used to complain to you all the time about how crowded our dormitory room was, and about all the things they did to irritate me, like watching movies late at night without headphones, or talking loudly early in the morning. But now I miss them terribly.
lines.zh: W: 我这么说听起来可能像个傻瓜，因为我以前总是向你抱怨我们的宿舍有多拥挤，还抱怨他们做的那些让我恼火的事，比如深夜不戴耳机看电影，或者一大早大声说话。可现在我特别想念他们。

lines.en: M: Of course you do. That's perfectly normal. When I got my first place I remember thinking I couldn't wait to live by myself and get away from my juvenile roommates and all their annoying habits. But then I began missing them and feeling lonely and thinking that our dormitory was like paradise, even though there were six of us guys in one small room.
lines.zh: M: 你当然会想念他们，这完全正常。我刚有自己的住处时，记得自己当时想的是，真等不及要独自生活，摆脱那些幼稚的室友和他们烦人的习惯。可是后来我开始想念他们，感到孤独，还觉得我们的宿舍简直像天堂，尽管我们六个大男人挤在一个小房间里。

lines.en: W: I thought it was just me who felt like that.
lines.zh: W: 我还以为只有我会有这种感觉。

lines.en: M: Look, you lived at home with us, and then you had three roommates, and this is your first time living alone. So it's hard. But your first apartment is a milestone in your life, and you should celebrate it. Tell me about the apartment.
lines.zh: M: 你以前和我们住在家里，后来又和三个室友一起住，而这是你第一次独居，所以确实很难适应。不过，你的第一套公寓是人生中的一个里程碑，你应该庆祝一下。跟我说说这套公寓吧。

lines.en: W: Actually, it's not bad. In fact, it's pretty adorable, now that I have decorated it and it has everything I need. I have a kitchen to cook in and a bathroom all to myself, and then another room with my bed at one end, and a sofa, a small table and chairs at the other end.
lines.zh: W: 其实，它还不错。事实上，我把它装饰好，也置办齐了所有需要的东西之后，发现它还挺可爱的。我有一间可以做饭的厨房和一间完全属于自己的浴室，另外还有一个房间，一头放着我的床，另一头放着沙发、小桌子和椅子。

lines.en: M: That does sound adorable and I can't wait to see it, and neither can mom and dad.
lines.zh: M: 听起来确实很可爱，我都等不及想去看看了，爸爸妈妈也一样。

lines.en: W: Welcome to our program Book Talk. Our guest today is Frank Jones, a critic of our education system, and the author of a new book, How to Reform Our Universities.
lines.zh: W: 欢迎收听我们的节目《图书访谈》。今天的嘉宾是弗兰克·琼斯，他是我们教育体系的批评者，也是新书《如何改革我们的大学》的作者。

lines.en: M: Hello, Susan.
lines.zh: M: 你好，苏珊。

lines.en: W: Frank, you support radically changing universities in America?
lines.zh: W: 弗兰克，你支持彻底改变美国的大学吗？

lines.en: M: Yes, I believe that the purpose of higher education is to prepare young people to enter the workforce, and that our current system fails to do this. We're allocating too many resources to disciplines that don't match the needs of employers.
lines.zh: M: 是的，我认为高等教育的目的是让年轻人为进入职场做好准备，而我们目前的体系没有做到这一点。我们把太多资源分配给了与雇主需求不匹配的学科。

lines.en: W: I think your attitude to education is a bit cynical, Frank. Surely the purpose of university is to prepare young people to participate fully in civic life, rather than just to find well-paid jobs.
lines.zh: W: 弗兰克，我觉得你对教育的态度有点愤世嫉俗。大学的目的当然应该是让年轻人充分参与公民生活，而不只是找到高薪工作。

lines.en: M: Susan, many young graduates struggle to find any job, let alone a good one. The job market is grim, particularly for students who study the arts.
lines.zh: M: 苏珊，许多年轻的毕业生连工作都很难找到，更不用说一份好工作了。就业市场很不景气，尤其是对学习艺术的学生而言。

lines.en: W: I agree that it isn't easy for young people to find work, but you propose closing down all departments that aren't directly related to science and technology. Is that really the solution?
lines.zh: W: 我同意年轻人找工作并不容易，但你提议关闭所有与科学和技术没有直接关系的院系。这真的是解决办法吗？

lines.en: M: You're overstating my point. My argument is that we need to use more of our budget on areas like science and engineering. To do that, we need to take money from subjects like literature and music.
lines.zh: M: 你夸大了我的观点。我的意思是，我们需要把更多预算用于科学和工程等领域。要做到这一点，我们就得从文学、音乐等学科中抽走资金。

lines.en: W: But the arts have value. They're an important part of our culture. Studying literature or music or sculpture might not result in a job in that area, but it helps young people to think about the world in a deeper way, which makes them better citizens and makes for a better society.
lines.zh: W: 但艺术是有价值的。它们是我们文化的重要组成部分。学习文学、音乐或雕塑也许不会让人最终从事相关领域的工作，但这能帮助年轻人更深入地思考世界，使他们成为更好的公民，也让社会变得更好。

lines.en: M: I agree that the arts are valuable to society, but it's naive to think that not only the most talented, but all students should study them at university level. The arts are very competitive, and most graduates will end up with a great deal of debt, obtaining a degree that has little value on the job market.
lines.zh: M: 我同意艺术对社会有价值，但认为不仅最有天赋的学生，所有学生都应该在大学阶段学习艺术，这种想法很天真。艺术领域竞争非常激烈，大多数毕业生最终会背负巨额债务，拿到一个在就业市场上价值不大的学位。

lines.en: Do you ever have the annoying feeling that you don't have time to really think anymore? You are not alone. A variety of factors have conspired to rob us of time for reflection about ourselves and our lives. Today, our preoccupied minds are rarely silent. The average person receives hundreds of texts and voice messages a day, and holidays for many of us are action-packed weeks more likely full of family activities than opportunities for tranquility and contemplation.
lines.zh: 你是否常有一种恼人的感觉，觉得自己再也没有时间真正思考了？你并不孤单。各种因素共同作用，夺走了我们用于反思自己和生活的时间。如今，我们被各种事务占据的头脑很少有安静的时候。普通人每天会收到数百条短信和语音消息，而对我们许多人来说，假期也是安排得满满当当的一周，更多的是充满家庭活动，而不是拥有宁静与沉思的机会。

lines.en: Regular reflection, however, underlies all great professionals. It's a prerequisite for you to recharge your mental batteries, see things in a new light and tap into your creativity. Almost all of the great advisors that I have studied have found ways to get away from it all and contemplate their life and work. Some researchers in the field of creativity, in fact, believe that insight occurs during the reflection and relaxation that follows a period of intense activity.
lines.zh: 然而，定期反思是一切杰出专业人士的基础。这是你重新充实心理能量、以新的眼光看待事物并发挥创造力的先决条件。我研究过的几乎所有杰出顾问，都找到了远离一切、思考自己生活和工作的方式。事实上，一些创造力领域的研究人员认为，洞见产生于高强度活动之后的反思与放松期间。

lines.en: Schedule time for reflection about your work or a particular project you're engaged in. I usually block out half an hour. Don't answer the phone. Push your papers to the side. Sketch, make lists, draw "mind maps" of ideas that come to you. At the end, write down any emerging ideas.
lines.zh: 安排时间反思你的工作或正在参与的某个项目。我通常会留出半小时。不要接电话。把文件推到一边。画草图、列清单、把浮现出的想法绘制成“思维导图”。最后，把任何新出现的想法记下来。

lines.en: When you're alone, stop worrying and think. A lot of our down time is spent worrying about troublesome things in our lives or fantasizing about how we'd like our lives to be. Revisit things during moments of relaxation after a period of intense work. This is when we are the most creative.
lines.zh: 独处时，停止担忧，认真思考。我们许多空闲时间都花在担心生活中令人烦恼的事情上，或幻想自己的生活应该是什么样子。在一段高强度工作之后的放松时刻，重新思考这些事情。此时正是我们最具创造力的时候。

lines.en: Even before Colorado was a state, it had post offices. The first opened in 1859, in a settlement founded by migrants searching for gold. Life could be unpredictable out west—gold failed to appear, drought ruined farmers and settlers clashed with Native Americans. On the settlement's location now stands a sprawling university campus. Amid all the changes, one feature remained constant—the postal service.
lines.zh: 甚至在科罗拉多成为一个州之前，这里就已经有了邮局。第一家邮局于1859年在一个由寻找黄金的移民建立的定居点开业。西部的生活充满不可预测性——黄金未能出现，干旱摧残了农民，移居者与美洲原住民发生冲突。在该定居点如今的位置上，耸立着一座庞大的大学校园。在所有的变迁中，有一个特征始终保持不变——那就是邮政服务。

lines.en: The maps tracing America's westward expansion are telling. In 1864, there were few postal branches on land controlled by Native Americans, which still accounted for most of the West. Over the next 25 years, post offices grew quickly. Colonization of the West could be regarded as a result of big government rather than pioneers. As federal subsidies and land grants tempted people into the deserts and plains, the post kept them connected.
lines.zh: 追溯美国西进运动的地图非常具有说服力。1864年，在美洲原住民控制的土地上几乎没有邮政分局，而这些土地当时仍占据了西部的大部分。在接下来的25年里，邮局迅速增多。对西部的拓殖可以被视为大政府而非拓荒者的产物。随着联邦补贴和土地赠予吸引人们深入沙漠和平原，邮政保持了他们之间的联系。

lines.en: In the mid-19th century, the Post Office Department was far from a centralized bureaucracy. To keep up with migration patterns, postal services were added to existing businesses. The federal government commissioned private wagons to carry the mail. Short-term contracts were granted to local businessmen to act as postmasters. These partnerships enabled the mail to quickly follow migrants, helping knit together remote parts of the country.
lines.zh: 在19世纪中叶，邮政部远非一个集权的官僚机构。为了跟上移民模式的脚步，邮政服务被附加到了现有的商业经营中。联邦政府委托私人马车运送邮件。当地商人获得了担任邮局局长的短期合同。这些合作关系使邮件能够迅速跟随移民，有助于将该国偏远地区紧密联系在一起。

lines.en: Mr. Blevins, a digital historian, wrote a book on the history of the US postal service. He used data science to analyze historical trends. Most strikingly, he built an accompanying website, complete with interactive maps. They show readers how, within a generation, the postal service helped colonize a continent. These online interactive maps illustrate the formative power of snail mail.
lines.zh: 数字历史学家布莱文斯先生写了一本关于美国邮政服务历史的书。他利用数据科学分析了历史趋势。最引人注目的是，他建立了一个配套网站，里面配备了完整的互动地图。它们向读者展示了在短短一代人的时间内，邮政服务是如何协助拓殖整块大陆的。这些在线互动地图展示了传统邮政的塑造力量。

lines.en: In last week's lecture, we discussed reasons why people forget things. This week, we will discuss a surprising reason why we might remember some things—anxiety.
lines.zh: 在上周的讲座中，我们讨论了人们遗忘事物的原因。本周，我们将讨论一个令人惊讶的、可能使我们记住某些事物的原因——焦虑。

lines.en: Think about something as simple as buying a coffee. That may not seem like an experience that would make a deep impression on your memory, but anxiety could change that. In fact, a new study suggests that people with higher anxiety levels might remember certain information better than people with lower anxiety levels. That's because higher levels of anxiety may make people more susceptible to negative feelings, putting them in a more negative state of mind. That in turn may make them able to better remember some events.
lines.zh: 想一想像买咖啡这样简单的事情。这似乎不太像是一种会在记忆中留下深刻印象的经历，但焦虑可能会改变这一点。事实上，一项新的研究表明，焦虑程度较高的人可能比焦虑程度较低的人更能记住某些信息。这是因为较高程度的焦虑可能使人更容易受到负面情绪的影响，使他们处于更加消极的心理状态。这反过来可能使他们能够更好地记住某些事件。

lines.en: Let's take a closer look at that new study now. In the study, the researchers started by giving 80 undergraduate students an anxiety test. The test measured the participants' anxiety levels over the preceding two weeks. Then, to test memory, the participants were shown a series of neutral words, one at a time. Some of the words were printed on to photos of negative scenes, meaning images that could affect their emotions negatively, such as a photo of a car accident or a cemetery. The rest of the words were printed on to photos of neutral scenes, such as a photo of a lake or trees. Neutral words included words like "table" or "desk" that don't elicit emotion. Later, the participants were asked to think back to the words they were shown earlier, which caused them to reenter either a negative or a neutral mindset. The participants were then presented with another set of neutral words, and their memory of these new words was tested.
lines.zh: 现在让我们更仔细地了解一下这项新研究。在这项研究中，研究人员首先让80名本科生接受焦虑测试。该测试测量了参与者在此前两周内的焦虑程度。随后，为了测试记忆力，研究人员让参与者逐一观看一系列中性词语。其中一些词语印在负面场景的照片上，也就是可能对他们的情绪产生负面影响的图像上，例如车祸或墓地的照片。其余词语则印在中性场景的照片上，例如湖泊或树木的照片。中性词语包括“桌子”或“书桌”之类不会引发情绪的词语。之后，研究人员要求参与者回想刚才看到的词语，这使他们重新进入消极或中性的心理状态。然后，研究人员向参与者展示另一组中性词语，并测试他们对这些新词语的记忆。

lines.en: The researchers found that the new words presented to people in a negative mindset were better remembered by people with higher levels of anxiety than those with lower levels of anxiety. In other words, when highly anxious individuals took in otherwise emotionally neutral information that was presented to them, it became colored by their negative mindset, making them remember the information better. But these same effects were not seen in people with low levels of anxiety.
lines.zh: 研究人员发现，对于处于消极心理状态的人，新呈现的词语中，焦虑程度较高的人比焦虑程度较低的人记得更好。换句话说，高度焦虑的人接收到原本在情感上中性的信息时，这些信息会受到其消极心理状态的影响，从而使他们更好地记住这些信息。但在焦虑程度较低的人身上并未观察到同样的效果。

lines.en: Previous studies have found that extreme levels of anxiety, such as those experienced by people diagnosed with an anxiety disorder, can be quite detrimental to memory and cognitive performance. But the highly anxious people in this study represent individuals who are managing their anxiety and for whom anxiety is not a serious problem.
lines.zh: 先前的研究发现，极高程度的焦虑，例如被诊断患有焦虑障碍的人所经历的焦虑，可能会严重损害记忆力和认知表现。但这项研究中的高度焦虑者代表的是那些能够管理自己的焦虑、且焦虑并非严重问题的人。

lines.en: Over the past 20 years, the internet has gradually become a dominant feature of our lives. It has changed how we communicate with each other, and it has definitely transformed the way we do business with each other. Marketing has also changed in a number of ways. For instance, in the past, consumers had to call a phone number and patiently wait on hold, in order to get the information they wanted. Today, they want the information immediately. They'll go to the company's social media page and post comments and questions, expecting to receive an immediate response. If they don't get their questions answered soon, they'll move on to another company that will answer them quickly.
lines.zh: 在过去20年里，互联网逐渐成为我们生活中的主导因素。它改变了我们彼此沟通的方式，也确实改变了我们彼此开展业务的方式。营销也在许多方面发生了变化。例如，过去，消费者必须拨打一个电话号码，并耐心等待接通，才能获得他们想要的信息。如今，他们希望立即获得信息。他们会前往公司的社交媒体页面，发布评论和问题，并期待立即得到回应。如果他们的问题很快得不到解答，就会转而选择另一家能够迅速回答他们问题的公司。

lines.en: Marketing departments today need to follow technological development. For example, this year's smartphone is smarter than last year's; self-driving cars are now on the road. Marketers have to do research on which technologies are coming into being. Otherwise, they risk being left behind in the virtual dust. Marketing has also changed due to the importance of video. People don't just want to read text; they want to watch things happening. Companies now have to explore how they can use video on a consistent basis to share information about their businesses. Fortunately, it's extremely easy to shoot something these days. All you need is a smartphone.
lines.zh: 如今，营销部门需要跟上技术的发展。例如，今年的智能手机比去年的更智能；自动驾驶汽车如今已经上路。营销人员必须研究哪些技术正在出现，否则就有被抛在虚拟尘埃中的风险。营销也因视频的重要性而发生了变化。人们不只是想阅读文字；他们还想观看事情发生的过程。如今，公司必须探索如何持续利用视频来分享有关自身业务的信息。幸运的是，现在拍摄视频非常容易。你只需要一部智能手机。

lines.en: But what's the result of all this? Shorter attention spans. We aren't the same people that we were 20 years ago. Not only have we grown accustomed to getting the information we want instantaneously, our attention spans are much shorter. If something doesn't capture our attention within a few seconds, we're on to the next piece of content. Marketers need to figure out ways to speak directly to the customers' emotions, and they need to figure out how to do that as quickly as possible. Once people are emotionally engaged, they'll stick with you.
lines.zh: 但这一切带来了什么结果呢？注意力持续时间变短了。我们已经不是20年前的那群人了。我们不仅已经习惯于即时获得想要的信息，注意力持续时间也短得多了。如果某件事在几秒钟内无法吸引我们的注意力，我们就会转向下一条内容。营销人员需要想办法直接与客户的情感沟通，也需要想办法尽快做到这一点。一旦人们在情感上投入其中，他们就会一直关注你。

lines.en: If marketing has changed this much in the past 20 years, imagine what the next 20 years will bring. In a recent survey, only 9% of marketers could say with confidence that their marketing efforts were actually working. Their confidence is being shaken, because the rules of the game change every year. That's why it's important for marketers to pay attention to the latest technological developments and consider collaborating with technological innovators. That way, they'll be moving at the same pace as the tech industry.
lines.zh: 如果营销在过去20年里发生了如此大的变化，想象一下未来20年会带来什么。在最近的一项调查中，只有9%的营销人员能够自信地说，他们的营销工作确实奏效了。他们的信心正在受到动摇，因为游戏规则每年都在变化。这就是营销人员关注最新技术发展并考虑与技术创新者合作十分重要的原因。这样一来，他们就能与科技行业保持同样的步调。

lines.en: You might be surprised to learn that the benefits of friendships extend beyond people's social life and into their work, which is interesting when considering the extent to which people sacrifice friendships, or at least the time they spend with friends, because of the extended hours they're devoting to work. Just last week, I was remarking to a colleague that I'm content with only one social engagement per week. But according to recent research, that's evidently not enough.
lines.zh: 你可能会惊讶地得知，友谊带来的益处不仅限于人们的社交生活，还延伸到了工作领域。想到人们常常因为投入工作、延长工作时间，而牺牲友谊，或者至少牺牲与朋友相处的时间，这一点就很有意思。就在上周，我还对一位同事说，我每周只参加一次社交活动就满足了。但根据最近的研究，显然这还不够。

lines.en: In an initial study of more than 700 respondents, scholars from an American university analyzed the impact that friends, as opposed to family, have on self-esteem and well-being. Friends came out substantially on top. That's because to be someone's mate is a voluntary act, unlike family who people rarely get to choose. The researchers found that when people choose to cultivate and maintain supportive friendships with an individual, it means that the person is valued and worthy of their limited time. Such sentiments of value and worthiness boost our self-esteem.
lines.zh: 在一项对700多名受访者进行的初步研究中，一所美国大学的学者分析了朋友相较于家人对自尊和幸福感的影响。结果显示，朋友的影响明显更大。这是因为，成为某人的朋友是一种自愿行为，而家人通常并不是人们可以选择的。研究人员发现，当人们选择与某个人培养并维持相互支持的友谊时，这意味着那个人受到重视，值得人们投入有限的时间。这种受到重视和认可的感受会提升我们的自尊。

lines.en: The second study comprised more than 300 participants. It proved that the better we feel about ourselves, the more likely we'll perform our job confidently and competently. This follow-up study found that non-work friends even improve people's job satisfaction. They have as much of an impact on how much they love their jobs as do the friends they have at work, despite not actually being at our place of work. These types of friends tend to be our preferred outlet for venting about work-related matters. This is an avenue that may not be available at the office.
lines.zh: 第二项研究由300多名参与者组成。研究证明，我们对自己的感觉越好，就越有可能自信而出色地完成工作。这项后续研究发现，工作之外的朋友甚至还能提高人们的工作满意度。尽管这些朋友并不在我们的工作场所，但他们对我们有多喜欢自己的工作所产生的影响，与工作中的朋友一样大。这类朋友往往是我们倾诉工作相关事情的首选对象，而在办公室里未必有这样的倾诉渠道。

lines.en: So even though friendships can be easy to neglect when confronted by pressures at work, or even pressures at home, neglecting our friends can turn out to be harmful and counterproductive. That's why, when determining how to create a better work-life balance, we need to consider not only how to balance work and family demands, but also how to cultivate and sustain supportive friendships. It's for this reason that managers should never discriminate when it comes to requests from employees for flexible work arrangements. It's irrelevant whether their need for a desired schedule is due to, say, parenting responsibilities, or a craving to hang out with a best mate. What matters is the opportunity to engage in a nourishing activity outside of work. That will definitely have a follow-on effect at work.
lines.zh: 因此，尽管在工作压力甚至家庭压力面前，友谊很容易被忽视，但忽视朋友最终可能会带来伤害，并产生适得其反的效果。这就是为什么，在确定如何实现更好的工作与生活平衡时，我们不仅需要考虑如何平衡工作和家庭的要求，还需要考虑如何培养并维持相互支持的友谊。正因如此，管理者在员工提出弹性工作安排请求时，绝不应区别对待。无论他们希望采用某种工作时间安排是因为需要承担育儿责任，还是因为想与最要好的朋友出去相聚，这都无关紧要。重要的是，他们有机会参与工作之外有益身心的活动。这肯定会对工作产生后续影响。

questions.stem: 【题目】 What does the man believe is the problem with the current American system of higher education?

analysis.定位: P4 I believe that the purpose of higher education is to prepare young people to enter the workforce, and that our current system fails to do this. 我认为高等教育的目的是让年轻人为进入职场做好准备，而我们现行的体制没能做到这一点。

analysis.替换: prepare young people to enter the workforce↔It has not prepared young people for the job market.workforce=job market
analysis.排除: A)原词陷阱It fails to keep up with the radical changes of society. 借用了原文 radically changing（radically changing universities）的 radical，但男方批的是“没对接就业”，并未说制度“跟不上社会的剧变”，把原词拼到一个原文没说的归因上。 借用原文：radically changing universities B)与原文相反It fails to ensure universities get sufficient resources. 盗用原文 resources（allocating too many resources）。男方说的是资源“分配错地方（过多给了不匹配需求的学科）”，不是大学“拿不到足够资源”，方向正相反。 借用原文：allocating too many resources to disciplines that don't match the needs of employers D)与原文相反It has not fostered the growth of the arts disciplines.（没扶持文科）与男方立场完全相反：他主张少投文科、多投理工（take money from subjects like literature and music），怎会嫌文科扶持不够。这是把他的对立面安到他头上。 借用原文：take money from subjects like literature and music

analysis.定位: P8 My argument is that we need to use more of our budget on areas like science and engineering. To do that, we need to take money from subjects like literature and music. 我的主张是，我们需要把更多预算用在科学和工程这类领域。要做到这一点，我们就得从文学、音乐这类科目那里抽走经费。

analysis.替换: use more of our budget on areas like science and engineering↔More of the budget should go to science and technology.“多用预算于”=“更多预算应给”
analysis.排除: B)与原文相反The underfunded music discipline should be prioritized. 盗用原文 music（literature and music）。男方恰恰主张从 music 抽钱（take money from），而非优先扶持 music，方向完全相反。 借用原文：take money from subjects like literature and music C)张冠李戴Subdisciplines like sculpture should get more funding. 借用女方后文提到的 sculpture（literature or music or sculpture）。但这是女方为艺术辩护时举的例，男方的主张是给理工加钱、从文科抽钱，绝不会主张给雕塑这类细分文科加经费，既张冠李戴又方向相反。 借用原文：Studying literature or music or sculpture D)偷换概念Literature should get as much funding as engineering. 盗用 literature、engineering 两个原词，却把男方“偏向理工、从文学抽钱”的不均等主张，偷换成“文学与工程经费同等”。男方要的是倾斜，不是均分。 借用原文：take money from subjects like literature and music

questions.stem: 【题目】 What does the passage say about Colorado before it became a state?

analysis.定位: P1 Even before Colorado was a state, it had post offices. The first opened in 1859, in a settlement founded by migrants searching for gold. 甚至在科罗拉多成为一个州之前，它就已经有了邮局。第一家邮局于 1859 年在一个由寻金移民建立的定居点开张。
analysis.信号: 开篇 before…was a state 直接点题。录音开篇即用 Even before Colorado was a state, it had post offices，before…a state 与题干完全对应，是直接给出事实的点题句，无需转折即可锁定。
analysis.替换: it had post offices↔There existed post offices.had 与 There existed 同义换说

questions.stem: 【题目】 How do marketers capture consumers' attention as quickly as possible?
questions.stem_zh: 营销人员如何尽快吸引消费者的注意力?

analysis.定位: P3 Marketers need to figure out ways to speak directly to the customers' emotions, and they need to figure out how to do that as quickly as possible. 营销者需要想办法直接打动顾客的情感，而且要想办法尽可能快地做到这一点。
analysis.信号: 建议信号 need to + 题干同词。Marketers need to figure out ways to 用 need to 给出明确做法，而且原句紧跟 as quickly as possible，和题干 as quickly as possible 逐字呼应，正是答案句。
analysis.替换: speak directly to the customers' emotions↔Speaking directly to their emotions几乎原句重述
analysis.排除: D)未提及Focusing on the details of the product 听起来像营销常识，但录音讲的是打动情感、是"人们想看视频而非读文字"，反而暗示不要堆细节文字，原文并未让营销者聚焦产品细节。 B)未提及Broadening their scope of interest 录音从未提及"拓宽消费者兴趣范围"，全篇讲的是注意力变短、要快速打动情感，方向不搭。 A)未提及Giving them rewards on the spot 的"当场给奖励"录音通篇未提，与"打动情感、抓住短暂注意力"的主线无关。

questions.stem_zh: 说话者建议营销人员做什么来应对未来的挑战?

analysis.定位: P4 That's why it's important for marketers to pay attention to the latest technological developments and consider collaborating with technological innovators. 这就是为什么营销者关注最新的技术发展、并考虑与技术创新者合作很重要。
analysis.信号: 结论信号 That's why + it's important。末段先讲未来挑战(信心被动摇、规则年年变)，再用 That's why it's important for marketers to 引出建议，That's why 加 it's important 是双重结论信号，这句即答案句。
analysis.替换: pay attention to the latest technological developments↔Keep up with the latest technological developmentspay attention to=keep up with 同义
analysis.排除: A)原词陷阱Change the rules of the game in the market every year 借了录音 the rules of the game change every year 的原话，但录音说的是"规则每年在变"(这是营销者面临的客观挑战/原因)，绝不是建议营销者"去改变规则"，把客观处境偷换成了主观建议。 借用原文：the rules of the game change every year C)原词陷阱Learn from technological innovators to do business 借了录音 collaborating with technological innovators 的"科技创新者"原词，但录音说的是"与之合作"(collaborating with)，不是"向其学习做生意"(learn from...to do business)，动作被偷换。 借用原文：collaborating with technological innovators D)原词陷阱Make greater efforts to build up consumers' confidence 借了录音 Their confidence is being shaken 的 confidence 原词，但原文说的是"营销者自己的信心被动摇"，根本不是"消费者的信心"，且讲者没建议去"建立消费者信心"，对象和建议双错。 借用原文：Their confidence is being shaken

questions.stem: 【题目】 What does the speaker say is interesting?
questions.stem_zh: 说话者认为什么是有趣的?

analysis.定位: P1 You might be surprised to learn that the benefits of friendships extend beyond people's social life and into their work, which is interesting when considering the extent to which people sacrifice friendships … because of the extended hours they're devoting to work. 你或许会惊讶地发现，友谊的好处不止于社交生活，还延伸进了工作之中；考虑到人们为了延长工作时间而牺牲友谊，这一点尤其有意思。
analysis.信号: interesting 一词所在句，即题干所指那句。录音里 which is interesting 的 interesting 与题干 interesting 完全对应，它前面那句 the benefits of friendships extend beyond people's social life and into their work 就是讲者说『有意思』的内容，这是直接的词面信号，听到 interesting 即锁定。
analysis.替换: the benefits of friendships extend beyond people's social life and into their work↔Friendships benefit work.『友谊好处延伸进工作』概括为『友谊有益工作』
analysis.排除: A)原词陷阱A:People have only one social engagement per week. 里的 one social engagement per week 是讲者后面 I'm content with only one social engagement per week 自述的个人情况，被搬来当选项，但题干问的是『什么有意思』，这只是讲者举的自身例子，答非所问。 借用原文：I'm content with only one social engagement per week B)与原文相反B:Working together enhances friendship. 说『一起工作增进友谊』，箭头是工作→友谊；而录音 the benefits of friendships … into their work 说的是友谊→工作。方向正好掉头，是预读时就提防的反向陷阱。 借用原文：the benefits of friendships extend beyond people's social life and into their work C)未提及C:Few people have devoted friends. 断言『很少有人有忠实朋友』，录音通篇在讲友谊的益处，从没下过这个数量上的极端论断，属凭空捏造。

questions.stem: 【题目】 What did researchers from an American university analyze in their initial study?
questions.stem_zh: 一所美国大学的研究人员在他们的初步研究中分析了什么?

analysis.定位: P2 In an initial study of more than 700 respondents, scholars from an American university analyzed the impact that friends, as opposed to family, have on self-esteem and well-being. 在一项有 700 多名受访者的初步研究中，一所美国大学的学者分析了朋友（相对于家人）对自尊与幸福感的影响。
analysis.信号: initial study + analyzed，题干用词逐字对应。录音 In an initial study … analyzed the impact that friends … have on self-esteem 把题干的 initial study、analyze 原样念出，这句就是首个研究的定义句；analyzed 后面跟的宾语即题干所问『分析了什么』，是直接的词面对应信号。
analysis.替换: the impact that friends, as opposed to family, have on self-esteem and well-being↔The impact of friends on people's self-esteem.原话与选项几乎同构，仅剪掉 well-being
analysis.排除: B)原词陷阱B:How supportive friends can be in the workplace. 里的 supportive、workplace 是录音别处出现过的词（如 supportive friendships），但首个研究分析的是 friends 对 self-esteem 的影响，不是『朋友在职场多支持』，张冠李戴。 借用原文：supportive friendships C)原词陷阱C:How to boost one's sense of value and worthiness. 用了录音 sentiments of value and worthiness boost our self-esteem 里的 value、worthiness，但那是研究推出的结论，不是研究『分析了什么』；且 C 把它说成『如何提升』，偷换成了方法问题，答非所问。 借用原文：Such sentiments of value and worthiness boost our self-esteem D)张冠李戴D:The role of family ties in people's mental well-being. 把 family 当成研究核心，但录音 friends, as opposed to family 里 family 只是用来反衬朋友的对照物，研究真正聚焦的是 friends，选 D 等于把配角当主角。 借用原文：friends, as opposed to family

locate.en: In an initial study of more than 700 respondents, scholars from an American university analyzed the impact that friends, as opposed to family, have on self-esteem and well-being.
locate.zh: 在一项有 700 多名受访者的初步研究中，一所美国大学的学者分析了朋友（相对于家人）对自尊与幸福感的影响。

questions.stem: 【题目】 What does the speaker suggest managers do?
questions.stem_zh: 说话者建议管理者做什么?

analysis.定位: P4 It's for this reason that managers should never discriminate when it comes to requests from employees for flexible work arrangements. 正因如此，管理者在面对员工提出的弹性工作安排请求时，绝不应区别对待。

analysis.替换: managers should never discriminate when it comes to requests from employees for flexible work arrangements↔Allow employees to have a flexible work schedule.『绝不区别对待弹性请求』正面化为『允许弹性安排』
analysis.排除: B)答非所问B:Encourage employees to be friends with colleagues. 把建议窄化成『鼓励和同事交朋友』，但录音 non-work friends even improve people's job satisfaction 一直强调非工作朋友的价值，讲者给管理者的建议是弹性安排，从没让管理者撮合同事交友，答非所问。 借用原文：non-work friends even improve people's job satisfaction C)原词陷阱C:Help employees balance work and family responsibilities. 搬用录音 how to balance work and family demands 的原词，但那是讲者谈 work-life balance 时的铺垫；他给管理者的落地建议是别歧视弹性安排请求，C 把铺垫当成了建议本身。 借用原文：how to balance work and family demands D)原词陷阱D:Organize activities to nourish friendships outside of work. 把录音 the opportunity to engage in a nourishing activity outside of work 的 nourishing、outside of work 原词搬来，听上去最耳熟，但录音说的是『员工有机会参与工作外的滋养性活动』，并没让管理者去『组织活动』；管理者要做的是别歧视弹性请求，张冠李戴又偷换了动作。 借用原文：What matters is the opportunity to engage in a nourishing activity outside of work

cloze.title: 2023年6月·第1套 英语六级完形填空（选词填空） · 26–35 题答案与解析

passages.en: Scientists recently examined studies on dog intelligence and compared them with research into the minds of other intelligent animals. The researchers found that dogs are among the more intelligent carnivores(食肉动物), social hunters and domestic animals, but that their intelligence does not __(26)__ other intelligent animals in any of those categories. Though a significant body of research has examined dog cognition __(27)__ , the authors of this new study found little to warrant the __(28)__ of work that has been devoted to the topic.
passages.zh: 科学家最近审阅了有关狗的智力的研究，并将其与对其他聪明动物心智的研究进行了比较。研究人员发现，狗属于较为聪明的食肉动物、群居猎手和家养动物，但在上述任何一个类别中，它们的智力都没有超过其他聪明动物。尽管此前已有大量研究考察了狗的认知能力，但这项新研究的作者发现，没有多少证据能够证明投入在这一主题上的研究数量是合理的。

passages.en: Stephen Lea, lead author of the new study, argues that many researchers seem to have designed their studies to __(29)__ how clever dogs are, rather than simply to study dogs' brains. Lea and a colleague examined more than 300 studies of dog cognition, comparing the studies' results with those from research into other animals. The researchers made specific comparisons between the different species in different categories of intelligence. These comparisons __(30)__ that dogs are intelligent, but their intelligence is not as __(31)__ as some researchers might have believed.
passages.zh: 这项新研究的主要作者斯蒂芬·利认为，许多研究人员似乎是为了证明狗有多聪明而设计研究的，而不是单纯研究狗的脑部。利和一位同事考察了300多项有关狗的认知能力的研究，并将这些研究的结果与对其他动物的研究结果进行了比较。研究人员针对不同类别的智力，对不同物种进行了具体比较。这些比较证实狗是聪明的，但它们的智力并不像一些研究人员可能认为的那样强大。

passages.en: In many areas, though, comparisons were not possible. For example, the researchers noted that both dogs and cats are known to be able to recognize and __(32)__ human voices. But the investigators could not find any data to indicate which species can remember a greater number of __(33)__ human voices, so it was impossible to compare the two on that front. However, not all researchers agree __(34)__ with the findings of this study. Zachary Silver, an American researcher, believes the authors of the new study __(35)__ the idea that an excessive amount of research has been devoted to dogs, as the field of dog cognition is young, and there is much to be learned about how dogs think.
passages.zh: 不过，在许多方面，研究人员无法进行比较。例如，研究人员指出，已知狗和猫都能够识别并区分人的声音。但调查人员找不到任何数据来表明哪一种动物能够记住数量更多的不同人声，因此无法在这一方面对二者进行比较。然而，并非所有研究人员都完全认同这项研究的结论。美国研究人员扎卡里·西尔弗认为，这项新研究的作者夸大了有关针对狗的研究过多这一观点，因为狗的认知研究领域还很年轻，人们对于狗的思维方式仍有许多需要了解的地方。

wordbank.gloss: 肯定、证实（过去式/过去分词）
不同的、独特的、清晰可辨的
令人敬畏的、强大的、了不起的
胜过、表现优于（过去式/过去分词）
夸大、言过其实（过去式/过去分词）

rows.text: N) surpass动词
does not 后接动词原形

“并不超过其他聪明动物”照应主旨 前句说 dogs are among the more intelligent carnivores(食肉动物), social hunters and domestic animals，下半句用 but 转折，意思必然是“但并不在这些类别里 X 其他聪明动物”。surpass 表“超过、胜过”，正合“狗虽聪明但并未超越同类”的论断，与第二段 their intelligence is not as __(31)__ as some researchers might have believed 互相印证。

D)differentiate“区分”后通常接 between/from differentiate 表“区分”，差异辨别义，与 intelligence does not differentiate other animals 搭不上；且 D 另有去处（见 32 题“辨别人声”）。 J)pledge“保证”不接动物作宾 pledge 表“承诺、保证”，主语必须是人或机构，intelligence 作主语不能 pledge animals，语义彻底错位。 M)prove“证明其他动物”逻辑断裂 prove 后通常接 that 从句或形容词补足语；intelligence does not prove other animals 不构成完整意思，且 M 另有去处（见 29 题）。

最具迷惑性的错误词是 H) —— outperformed 词义近、形态却错。outperformed 意为“胜过”，词义几乎与 surpass 一致，最容易被误选进 their intelligence does not __(26)__ other intelligent animals。一句话防坑：does not 后必跟动词原形，outperformed 是过去分词/过去式，词形先被淘汰。
K) previously副词
完成时谓语后修饰动词的状语位
与完成时呼应的“此前已研究” has examined 现在完成时强调“到目前为止已有研究”，previously 表“先前、以前”，正好对应“此前已有大量研究考察过狗的认知”，与下半句 found little to warrant the __(28)__ of work 形成“前人研究虽多、却未必必要”的转折逻辑。

B)approximately近似义不修饰研究行为 approximately 表“大约”，通常修饰数字或量，如 approximately 300，不会用来修饰 examined 这种研究动作。 C)completely“完全考察”语义荒谬且与下文矛盾 completely 表“彻底地”，说“研究已经彻底考察了狗的认知”与下句“认为投入的工作量并不值得”自相矛盾；且 C 另有去处（见 34 题）。
O) volume名词
the 与 of 短语之间的名词中心词

“工作量之多”才能被 warrant 衡量 warrant 意为“证明…是必要/正当的”，宾语应是某种可被衡量的“量”。volume 表“数量、规模”，the volume of work 即“工作量”，承接前文 Though a significant body of research has examined dog cognition __(27)__ 中的 a significant body of research，呼应“研究量之大是否值得”的主线，是全文论点的关键词。
F)domain“工作领域”与 warrant 搭不上 domain 表“领域”，the domain of work 听上去是“工作的领域”，但 warrant the domain of work（证明这一工作领域的合理性）逻辑别扭，且与下文“量”的比较主题不符。
M) prove动词
不定式 to 后接动词原形
“证明狗有多聪明”而非客观研究 本句关键是对比 to __(29)__ how clever dogs are, rather than simply to study dogs' brains——前后是“证明 vs 研究”的对立。prove 后接 how 从句意为“证明狗有多聪明”，恰好讽刺这些研究的预设立场，与后文“狗其实没那么 formidable”的反转呼应。
D)differentiate“区分”不带 how 从句 differentiate 后跟 between/from + 名词，不接 how clever dogs are 这类问句式从句。 J)pledge“承诺狗有多聪明”不合事理 pledge 是“承诺/誓言”，研究者不会“承诺狗多聪明”，逻辑荒谬。
A) affirmed动词
主语后缺谓语
“比较结果证实了…”最贴合 affirmed 表“证实、肯定”，后接 that 从句意为“这些比较证实了…”，与上句 Lea and a colleague examined more than 300 studies of dog cognition 形成“做完比较→得出结论”的因果衔接，承接自然。

H)outperformed“胜过”宾语应是对手而非从句 outperformed 表“胜过”，宾语应为竞争对象（人或物），不接 that 从句；comparisons outperformed that... 不成句。 I)overstated“夸大”后接概念名词，不接“狗聪明”这种事实从句 overstated 表“夸大”，宾语多为 risk、importance、case 等抽象名词，主语 these comparisons 也不会“夸大”自身得出的事实；且 I 另有去处（见 35 题）。
G) formidable形容词
系动词 as 后的形容词作表语

“没有大家想的那么了不起” 整段在质疑“狗的智力被高估”：dogs are intelligent, but their intelligence is not as __(31)__ as some researchers might have believed。formidable 表“令人敬畏的、了不起的”，与 intelligent 同向但程度更强，正好对应“没研究者以为得那么强”的反差。
L)prospective“潜在的智力”与同级比较语义错位 prospective 表“未来的、有望的”，多修饰人或角色（prospective student/buyer），不修饰 intelligence；且与 as...as 比较“以前有多相信”逻辑不通。
最具迷惑性的错误词是 E) —— distinct 在 33 题用过、勿用过即划失败。distinct 也是形容词、且“独特的智力”乍听通顺，主体考生若没坚持“用过即划”，容易在 31 题二次选 E，导致 33 题反而崩盘。防坑：每填一空立刻在草稿上划掉该字母。
D) differentiate动词
情态动词 + 并列动词原形

与 recognize 并列形成“识别+辨别” recognize 是“认出”，differentiate 是“辨别（区分不同的）”，二者构成“识别并区分人声”的常见认知能力描述，且呼应下句 remember a greater number of __(33)__ human voices 中 distinct 的“不同”主题——能 differentiate 才谈得上记住多少 distinct voices。
J)pledge“狗保证人声”完全不通 pledge 表“承诺、立誓”，主语是猫狗、宾语是人声，无法构成任何合理含义。
E) distinct形容词
名词前作定语
“不同的人声”才好谈“记住多少种” 本句讨论 which species can remember a greater number of __(33)__ human voices，要比较谁能记住更多“不同的”人声。distinct 意为“截然不同的、可分辨的”，与 a greater number of 搭配自然，正好突出“记住的人声种类多寡”这一比较点。
G)formidable“强大的人声”不通 formidable 多形容“令人生畏的对手/任务”，搭配 voices 在语义和搭配上都怪异；且 G 另有去处（见 31 题）。 L)prospective“潜在的人声”逻辑跑偏 prospective 表“未来的、潜在的”，多修饰 buyer、employer、student 这类“未来角色”，与“记住已经听过的人声数量”这个语境不搭。
C) completely副词
助动词 do 与实义动词 agree 之间的状语
“完全同意”与下文反对意见呼应 原文紧接出现 Zachary Silver, an American researcher, believes the authors of the new study __(35)__ the idea，表明确有研究者持不同看法。因此“并非所有研究者都 completely（完全）赞同这一结论”最贴切——not...completely 是地道的部分否定表达。
B)approximately“大约同意”不像人话 approximately 表数量上的近似，不与 agree 搭配；agree approximately with 不是英语习语。
I) overstated动词
主语 + 谓语 + 宾语的过去式动词

“夸大了‘狗研究过多’的论断”才符合反对者立场 Zachary Silver 持反对意见，认为新研究 the authors of the new study __(35)__ the idea that an excessive amount of research has been devoted to dogs, as the field of dog cognition is young, and there is much to be learned——下半句给出原因（领域年轻、还有很多要学），正是为了说明新研究“言过其实”。overstated 表“夸大”，与 overstated the idea/case 是固定搭配，精准命中。
H)outperformed“胜过观点”搭配荒谬 outperformed 表“在表现上胜过”，宾语应是竞争者；overperform the idea 不构成英语表达，与反对立场也无关。

longreading.title: 2023年6月·第1套 英语六级长篇阅读（信息匹配） 第 1 篇 · 36–45 题答案与解析

passages.en: A) Gratitude may be more beneficial than we commonly suppose. One recent study asked participants to write a note of thanks to someone and then estimate how surprised and happy the recipient would feel—an impact that they consistently underestimated. Another study assessed the health benefits of writing thank-you notes. The researchers found that writing as few as three weekly thank-you notes over the course of three weeks improved life satisfaction, increased happy feelings and reduced symptoms of depression.
passages.zh: 感恩可能比我们通常认为的更有益处。最近的一项研究要求参与者给某人写一封感谢信，然后估计收信人会感到多么惊讶和高兴，而参与者始终低估了这种影响。另一项研究评估了写感谢信对健康的益处。研究人员发现，在三周内每周写三封感谢信，就能提高生活满意度，增加愉快情绪，并减轻抑郁症状。

passages.en: B) While this research into gratitude is relatively new, the principles involved are anything but. Students of mine in a political philosophy course at Indiana University are reading Daniel Defoe's 300-year-old Robinson Crusoe, often regarded as the first novel published in English. Left alone on an unknown island with no apparent prospect of rescue or escape, Crusoe has much to lament(悲叹). But instead of giving in to despair, he makes a list of things for which he is grateful, including the fact that he is the sole survivor from the shipwreck(海难) and has been able to salvage many useful items from the wreckage.
passages.zh: 虽然对感恩的这类研究相对较新，但其中涉及的原则却绝非新鲜。我的一些印第安纳大学政治哲学课学生正在阅读丹尼尔·笛福三百年前创作的《鲁滨逊漂流记》，这部作品通常被认为是用英语出版的第一部小说。鲁滨逊独自一人被困在一座陌生岛屿上，显然没有获救或逃脱的希望，有许多事情值得悲叹。但他没有陷入绝望，而是列出了一些值得感恩的事情，其中包括自己是这场海难中唯一的幸存者，并且能够从残骸中抢救出许多有用的物品。

passages.en: C) Defoe's masterpiece, which is often ranked as one of the world's greatest novels, provides a portrait of gratitude in action that is as timely and relevant today as it has ever been. It is also one with which contemporary psychology and medicine are just beginning to catch up. Simply put, for most of us, it is far more helpful to focus on the things in life for which we can express gratitude than those that incline us toward resentment and lamentation.
passages.zh: 笛福的这部杰作常被列为世界上最伟大的小说之一，它描绘了感恩付诸实践的样子；无论过去还是现在，这一描绘都同样及时而贴切。这也是当代心理学和医学才刚刚开始追赶上的认识。简而言之，对我们大多数人来说，把注意力集中在生活中值得我们表达感恩的事情上，远比集中在那些容易使我们产生怨恨和悲叹的事情上更有益。

passages.en: D) When we focus on the things we regret, such as failed relationships, family disputes, and setbacks in career and finance, we tend to become more regretful. Conversely, when we focus on the things we are grateful for, a greater sense of happiness tends to spread through our lives. And while no one would argue for cultivating a false sense of blessedness, there is mounting evidence that counting our blessings is one of the best habits we can develop to promote mental and physical health.
passages.zh: 当我们把注意力集中在令人遗憾的事情上，例如失败的感情、家庭争端以及事业和经济上的挫折时，我们往往会变得更加遗憾。相反，当我们关注值得感恩的事情时，更强烈的幸福感往往会在我们的生活中扩散开来。虽然没有人会主张培养一种虚假的蒙福感，但越来越多的证据表明，数算自己的福分是我们能够养成的、促进身心健康的最佳习惯之一。

passages.en: E) Gratitude has long enjoyed a privileged position in many of the world's cultural traditions. For example, some ancient Western philosophers counsel gratitude that is both enduring and complete, and some Eastern thinkers portray it as not merely an attitude but a virtue to be put into practice.
passages.zh: 长期以来，感恩在世界上许多文化传统中都享有重要地位。例如，一些古代西方哲学家劝导人们保持持久而完整的感恩，而一些东方思想家则将感恩描述为不仅是一种态度，更是一种需要付诸实践的美德。

passages.en: F) Recent scientific studies support these ancient teachings. Individuals who regularly engage in gratitude exercises, such as counting their blessings or expressing gratitude to others, exhibit increased satisfaction with relationships and fewer symptoms of physical illness. And the benefits are not only psychological and physical. They may also be moral—those who practice gratitude also view their lives less materialistically and suffer from less envy.
passages.zh: 近期的科学研究支持了这些古老的教诲。经常进行感恩练习的人，例如数算自己的福分或向他人表达感恩的人，对人际关系的满意度更高，身体疾病的症状也更少。而且，感恩带来的益处不仅限于心理和身体层面，也可能具有道德意义：实践感恩的人对生活的物质主义看法较少，也较少遭受嫉妒之苦。

passages.en: G) There are multiple explanations for such benefits of gratefulness. One is the fact that expressing gratitude encourages others to continue being generous, thus promoting a virtuous cycle of goodness in relationships. Similarly, grateful people may be more likely to reciprocate(回报) with acts of kindness of their own. Broadly speaking, a community in which people feel grateful to one another is likely to be a more pleasant place to live than one characterized by mutual suspicion and resentment. The beneficial effects of gratitude may extend even further. For example, when many people feel good about what someone else has done for them, they experience a sense of being lifted up, with a corresponding enhancement of their regard for humanity. Some are inspired to attempt to become better people themselves, doing more to help bring out the best in others and bringing more goodness into the world around them.
passages.zh: 感恩能带来这些益处，有多种解释。其中一个原因是，表达感恩会鼓励他人继续慷慨相待，从而推动人际关系中善意的良性循环。同样，感恩的人也更有可能以自己的善举作出回报。总的来说，一个人们彼此心怀感恩的社区，很可能比一个充满相互猜疑和怨恨的社区更宜居。感恩的有益影响甚至可能延伸得更远。例如，当许多人因他人为自己所做的事情而感到欣慰时，他们会产生一种受到鼓舞的感觉，同时更加尊重人性。有些人还会受到激励，努力使自己成为更好的人，更多地帮助激发他人最好的一面，并为周围的世界增添更多美好。

passages.en: H) Gratitude also tends to strengthen a sense of connection with others. When people want to do good things that inspire gratitude, the level of dedication in relationships tends to grow and relationships seem to last longer. And when people feel more connected, they are more likely to choose to spend their time with one another and demonstrate their feelings of affection in daily acts.
passages.zh: 感恩也往往会增强人与人之间的联结感。当人们希望做出能够激发感恩的善举时，人际关系中的投入程度往往会提高，关系似乎也能维持更长时间。而当人们感到彼此联系更加紧密时，他们更有可能选择与对方共度时光，并在日常行为中表达自己的 affection。

passages.en: I) Of course, acts of kindness can also foster discomfort. For example, if people feel they are not worthy of kindness or suspect that some ulterior(别有用心的) motive lies behind it, the benefits of gratitude will not be realized. Likewise, receiving a kindness can give rise to a sense of indebtedness, leaving beneficiaries feeling that they must now pay back whatever good they have received. Gratitude can flourish only if people are secure enough in themselves and sufficiently trusting to allow it to do so. Another obstacle to gratitude is often called a sense of entitlement. Instead of experiencing a benefaction(善行) as a good turn, people sometimes regard it as a mere payment of what they are owed, for which no one deserves any moral credit.
passages.zh: 当然，善举也可能引起不适。例如，如果人们觉得自己不配得到善意，或者怀疑善意背后隐藏着某种别有用心的动机，那么感恩的益处就无法实现。同样，接受善意可能会产生亏欠感，使受惠者觉得自己现在必须偿还所得到的一切好处。只有当人们对自我足够安心，并且足够信任他人，感恩才会蓬勃发展。感恩的另一个障碍通常被称为应得感。人们有时并不把一项善行看作善意之举，而只是把它视为他人偿还自己应得之物，因此认为没有人值得因此获得道德上的赞誉。

passages.en: J) There are a number of practical steps anyone can take to promote a sense of gratitude. One is simply spending time on a regular basis thinking about someone who has made a difference, or perhaps writing a thank-you note or expressing such gratitude in person. Others are found in ancient religious disciplines, such as reflecting on benefactions received from another person or actually praying for the health and happiness of a benefactor. In addition to benefactions received, it is also possible to focus on opportunities to do good oneself, whether those acted on in the past or hoped for in the future. Some people are most grateful not for what others have done for them but for chances they enjoyed to help others. In regularly reflecting on the things in his life he is grateful for, Defoe's Crusoe believes that he becomes a far better person than he would have been had he remained in the society from which he originally set out on his voyage.
passages.zh: 任何人都可以采取一些切实可行的步骤来培养感恩意识。其中一种方法很简单，就是定期花时间想一想曾经对自己产生过影响的人，或者写一封感谢信，或当面表达这样的感激之情。其他方法则见于古老的宗教修行，例如回想他人给予自己的善行，或实际为施恩者的健康和幸福祈祷。除了关注自己所得到的善行，人们也可以关注亲自做好事的机会，无论是过去已经把握住的机会，还是未来所希望拥有的机会。有些人最感恩的并不是别人为自己做了什么，而是自己曾有机会帮助别人。笛福笔下的鲁滨逊定期回想生活中值得感恩的事情，他相信，正是这样使自己成为了一个远比原本留在出发航海前的社会中更好的人。

passages.en: K) Reflecting on generosity and gratitude, the great basketball coach John Wooden once offered two counsels to his players and students. First, he said, "It is impossible to have a perfect day unless you have done something for someone who will never be able to repay you." In saying this, Wooden sought to promote purely generous acts, as opposed to those performed with an expectation of reward. Second, he said, "Give thanks for your blessings every day."
passages.zh: 伟大的篮球教练约翰·伍登曾在思考慷慨与感恩时，向他的球员和学生提出过两条忠告。第一，他说：“除非你为一个永远无法偿还你的人做了某件事，否则你不可能拥有完美的一天。”伍登这样说，是为了倡导纯粹的慷慨行为，而不是带着期待回报的动机去行善。第二，他说：“每天都要为你所拥有的福分而感谢。”

passages.en: L) Some faith traditions incorporate such practices into the rhythm of daily life. For example, adherents of some religions offer prayers of thanksgiving every morning before rising and every night before lying down to sleep. Others offer thanks throughout the day, such as before meals. Other less frequent special events, such as births, deaths and marriages, may also be heralded by such prayers.
passages.zh: 一些信仰传统将这样的实践融入日常生活的节奏之中。例如，一些宗教的信徒每天早晨起床前和晚上躺下睡觉前都会进行感恩祈祷。还有一些人一整天都会表达感谢，例如在用餐前。其他较不频繁的特殊时刻，如出生、死亡和婚姻，也可能以这样的祈祷作为庆祝或纪念。

passages.en: M) When Defoe depicted Robinson Crusoe making thanksgiving a daily part of his island life, he was anticipating findings in social science and medicine that would not appear for hundreds of years. Yet he was also reflecting the wisdom of religious and philosophical traditions that extend back thousands of years. Gratitude is one of the healthiest and most nourishing of all states of mind, and those who adopt it as a habit are enriching not only their own lives but also the lives of those around them.
passages.zh: 当笛福描写鲁滨逊·克鲁索把感恩祈祷作为岛上生活的一部分、每天坚持时，他已经预见了数百年后才会出现的社会科学和医学研究发现。然而，他同时也反映了延续数千年的宗教和哲学传统中的智慧。感恩是所有心理状态中最有益健康、最能滋养心灵的状态之一，而把感恩培养成习惯的人，不仅丰富了自己的生活，也丰富了身边人的生活。

statements.en: It does us far more good to focus on things we can be grateful for than what makes us sad and resentful.
statements.zh: 关注那些我们能够感恩的事情比关注让我们悲伤和怨恨的事情对我们更有益。

analysis.锚点: 对比聚焦点的核心命题
analysis.定位: C 段 Simply put, for most of us, it is far more helpful to focus on the things in life for which we can express gratitude than those that incline us toward resentment and lamentation. 简单地说，对我们大多数人而言，专注于生活中那些值得感恩之事，远比专注于让人心生怨恨、悲叹之事更有益处。
analysis.改写: does us far more good↔far more helpful 比较级同义替换 focus on things we can be grateful for↔focus on the things in life for which we can express gratitude 动词到名词的同义改写 what makes us sad and resentful↔those that incline us toward resentment and lamentation 形容词与抽象名词的同义对换
analysis.辨邻: D When we focus on the things we regret… we tend to become more regretful 与 when we focus on the things we are grateful for, a greater sense of happiness tends to spread through our lives 只是分别从两端各说一面，没有把“X 远比 Y 更有益”这种比较关系整合在一句里；陈述句的 does us far more good 这一比较关系，只有 C 段的 far more helpful 直接承载。 When we focus on the things we regret, such as failed relationships, family disputes, and setbacks in career and finance, we tend to become more regretful. Conversely, when we focus on the things we are grateful for, a greater sense of happiness tends to spread through our lives.

statements.en: The beneficial impacts of gratitude can extend from individuals to their community and to the wider society.
statements.zh: 感恩的有益影响可以从个人延伸到他们的社区以及更广泛的社会。

analysis.锚点: 影响范围从个体扩散到社会
analysis.定位: G 段 Broadly speaking, a community in which people feel grateful to one another is likely to be a more pleasant place to live than one characterized by mutual suspicion and resentment. The beneficial effects of gratitude may extend even further. 总体来说，一个彼此感恩的社区，比一个充满相互猜忌与怨恨的社区更适合居住。感恩的有益影响甚至可能延伸得更远。
analysis.改写: individuals↔grateful people may be more likely to reciprocate 从抽象到具体的同义对应 community↔a community in which people feel grateful to one another 关键词原样复现 the wider society↔The beneficial effects of gratitude may extend even further 范围扩展的同义表达 beneficial impacts↔The beneficial effects of gratitude 近义词替换
analysis.辨邻: H Gratitude also tends to strengthen a sense of connection with others 与 they are more likely to choose to spend their time with one another 都停留在双人或小圈子的连接，没有出现 community/wider society 这样的范围扩张词，无法覆盖陈述句的“扩散至社区与更广社会”。 Gratitude also tends to strengthen a sense of connection with others. When people want to do good things that inspire gratitude, the level of dedication in relationships tends to grow and relationships seem to last longer. M those who adopt it as a habit are enriching not only their own lives but also the lives of those around them 只把益处扩到 those around them（周围他人），没有出现 community 或 wider society 的明确扩展。 those who adopt it as a habit are enriching not only their own lives but also the lives of those around them

statements.en: The participants in a recent study repeatedly underestimated the positive effect on those who received thank-you notes.
statements.zh: 最近一项研究中的参与者反复低估了感谢信对收信人产生的积极影响。

analysis.锚点: 一项新研究 + 反复低估收信人正面反应
analysis.定位: A 段 One recent study asked participants to write a note of thanks to someone and then estimate how surprised and happy the recipient would feel—an impact that they consistently underestimated. 最近一项研究让参与者给某人写一封感谢信，然后预估收信人会有多么惊讶与开心——而他们对这一影响始终估计得过低。
analysis.改写: The participants in a recent study↔One recent study asked participants 句式重构与关键词原样复现 those who received thank-you notes↔write a note of thanks to someone 角色视角互换 repeatedly underestimated the positive effect↔an impact that they consistently underestimated 近义副词与同根名词替换
analysis.辨邻: F Individuals who regularly engage in gratitude exercises, such as counting their blessings or expressing gratitude to others 描述的是常规感恩练习与人际关系/生理症状的关系，没有“写感谢信 + 预估收信人反应 + 持续低估”这一组实验细节。 Recent scientific studies support these ancient teachings. Individuals who regularly engage in gratitude exercises, such as counting their blessings or expressing gratitude to others, exhibit increased satisfaction with relationships and fewer symptoms of physical illness.

statements.en: Good deeds can sometimes make people feel uncomfortable.
statements.zh: 善行有时会让人感到不自在。

analysis.定位: I 段 Of course, acts of kindness can also foster discomfort. 当然，善举有时也会让人感到不适。
analysis.改写: Good deeds↔acts of kindness 同义替换 make people feel uncomfortable↔foster discomfort 形容词与同根名词的同义改写 sometimes↔can also 情态副词的同义对应

statements.en: People who regularly express gratitude can benefit in moral terms.
statements.zh: 经常表达感恩的人可以在道德方面受益。

analysis.锚点: 感恩带来道德层面的益处
analysis.定位: F 段 And the benefits are not only psychological and physical. They may also be moral—those who practice gratitude also view their lives less materialistically and suffer from less envy. 而且这些益处不仅是心理和生理上的，还可能是道德上的——践行感恩的人对生活的物质化看法更少、嫉妒心也更少。
analysis.改写: People who regularly express gratitude↔those who practice gratitude 近义动词与隐含的常态意思 benefit in moral terms↔They may also be moral 名词加修饰词与“系动词 + 形容词”的同义
analysis.辨邻: G expressing gratitude encourages others to continue being generous, thus promoting a virtuous cycle of goodness in relationships 谈的是关系层面的善意循环，Some are inspired to attempt to become better people themselves 偏“成为更好的人”，整体没有出现 moral 这个明确的道德维度词，与陈述句要求的 in moral terms 错位。 expressing gratitude encourages others to continue being generous, thus promoting a virtuous cycle of goodness in relationships

statements.en: A basketball coach advocated performing generous acts without expecting anything in return.
statements.zh: 一位篮球教练提倡做慷慨之举而不期待任何回报。

analysis.锚点: 篮球教练 + 不求回报
analysis.定位: K 段 In saying this, Wooden sought to promote purely generous acts, as opposed to those performed with an expectation of reward. 伍登说这番话，意在倡导纯粹的慷慨之举，而不是那些抱着期待回报心态去做的善行。
analysis.改写: A basketball coach↔the great basketball coach John Wooden 上位词到具体专名的同义对应 performing generous acts↔purely generous acts 动词化原文的名词短语 without expecting anything in return↔as opposed to those performed with an expectation of reward 把对照式表达压缩为否定修饰
analysis.辨邻: G expressing gratitude encourages others to continue being generous 与 grateful people may be more likely to reciprocate 谈的是慷慨与回报的循环，但通篇没有提及任何篮球教练，与陈述句明确要求的 a basketball coach 错位。 expressing gratitude encourages others to continue being generous, thus promoting a virtuous cycle of goodness in relationships. Similarly, grateful people may be more likely to reciprocate with acts of kindness of their own.

statements.en: More and more evidence shows it makes us mentally and physically healthier to routinely count our blessings.
statements.zh: 越来越多的证据表明,常规地数算我们的幸运会让我们在精神上和身体上更健康。

analysis.锚点: 越来越多证据 + 心身健康
analysis.定位: D 段 And while no one would argue for cultivating a false sense of blessedness, there is mounting evidence that counting our blessings is one of the best habits we can develop to promote mental and physical health. 尽管没人会主张刻意培养一种虚假的幸福感，但越来越多的证据表明，时常细数自己的福分是我们能养成的最佳习惯之一，对身心健康都有益。
analysis.改写: More and more evidence↔mounting evidence 近义形容词替换 routinely count our blessings↔counting our blessings is one of the best habits we can develop 副词与“习惯”概念的等值 mentally and physically healthier↔promote mental and physical health 形容词比较级与“促进健康”的同义
analysis.辨邻: F Recent scientific studies support these ancient teachings 只用 recent scientific studies 而非 mounting evidence；increased satisfaction with relationships and fewer symptoms of physical illness 侧重关系满意度与生理症状，没有同时出现“心理 + 生理健康”的双指纹。 Recent scientific studies support these ancient teachings. Individuals who regularly engage in gratitude exercises, such as counting their blessings or expressing gratitude to others, exhibit increased satisfaction with relationships and fewer symptoms of physical illness.

statements.en: Of all states of mind, feeling grateful is considered one of the most healthy and beneficial.
statements.zh: 在所有的心理状态中,感恩被认为是最健康和最有益的心态之一。

analysis.锚点: 感恩是最健康、最有益的心态之一
analysis.定位: M 段 Gratitude is one of the healthiest and most nourishing of all states of mind, and those who adopt it as a habit are enriching not only their own lives but also the lives of those around them. 感恩是所有心态中最健康、最滋养的心态之一；养成感恩习惯的人，不仅在丰盈自己的生活，也在丰盈身边人的生活。
analysis.改写: Of all states of mind↔of all states of mind 短语原样复现 feeling grateful↔Gratitude 动名词与抽象名词同义 one of the most healthy and beneficial↔one of the healthiest and most nourishing 最高级框架内的近义形容词替换
analysis.辨邻: D counting our blessings is one of the best habits we can develop to promote mental and physical health 中的 one of the best 修饰的是 habits，而陈述句要求 of all states of mind 中的最高级修饰对象是“心态”，对象错位即不构成匹配。 counting our blessings is one of the best habits we can develop to promote mental and physical health

statements.en: The principles underlying the research into gratitude are nothing new at all.
statements.zh: 感恩研究所依据的原则完全不是什么新事物。

analysis.锚点: 感恩研究背后的原理并不新
analysis.定位: B 段 While this research into gratitude is relatively new, the principles involved are anything but. 虽然这类关于感恩的研究相对较新，但其中所涉的原理一点都不新。
analysis.改写: The principles underlying the research into gratitude↔this research into gratitude is relatively new, the principles involved 句式重构与同义替换 are nothing new at all↔the principles involved are anything but 习语级强否定的同义
analysis.辨邻: E Gratitude has long enjoyed a privileged position in many of the world's cultural traditions 与 some ancient Western philosophers counsel gratitude 谈的是古代文化态度，没有出现“研究背后的原理一点都不新”这一对照句框架，与陈述句要求错位。 Gratitude has long enjoyed a privileged position in many of the world's cultural traditions.

statements.en: Gratitude is likely to enhance one's sense of being connected with other people.
statements.zh: 感恩很可能增强一个人与他人相连的感觉。

analysis.定位: H 段 Gratitude also tends to strengthen a sense of connection with others. 感恩也倾向于增强人与他人之间的连接感。
analysis.改写: is likely to enhance↔tends to strengthen 近义动词与情态副词同义 sense of being connected with other people↔sense of connection with others 动词过去分词与同根名词同义
analysis.辨邻: G a virtuous cycle of goodness in relationships 谈的是 relationships 中的善意循环，并未直接讲“增强连接感”；陈述句的“sense of being connected”需对 H 段的 sense of connection 主题句，与 G 段错位。 expressing gratitude encourages others to continue being generous, thus promoting a virtuous cycle of goodness in relationships.

reading1.title: 2023年6月·第1套 英语六级阅读理解（四选一） 第 1 篇 · 46–50 题答案与解析

passages.en: Technology is never a neutral tool for achieving human ends. Technological innovations reshape people as they use these innovations to control their environment. Artificial intelligence, for example, is altering humanity.
passages.zh: 技术从来都不是实现人类目的的中性工具。人们利用技术创新来控制环境的同时，这些创新也在重塑人类。例如，人工智能正在改变人类。

passages.en: While the term AI conjures up anxieties about killer robots or catastrophic levels of unemployment, there are other, deeper implications. As AI increasingly shapes the human experience, how does this change what it means to be human? Central to the problem is a person's capacity to make choices, particularly judgments that have moral implications.
passages.zh: 虽然“人工智能”这个词会让人联想到杀手机器人或灾难性程度的失业，但它还带来了其他更深层的影响。随着人工智能日益塑造人类的体验，这会如何改变“成为人类”的含义？问题的核心在于人的选择能力，尤其是作出具有道德影响的判断的能力。

passages.en: Aristotle argued that the capacity for making practical judgments depends on regularly making them—on habit and practice. We see the emergence of machines as substitute judges in a variety of everyday contexts as a potential threat to people learning how to effectively exercise judgment themselves.
passages.zh: 亚里士多德认为，作出实践判断的能力取决于经常作出这类判断，也就是说，取决于习惯和实践。我们认为，在各种日常情境中，机器作为替代性裁判的出现，可能会威胁到人们学习如何有效地自行行使判断力。

passages.en: In the workplace, managers routinely make decisions about who to hire or fire and which loan to approve, to name a few. These are areas where algorithmic(算法的) prescription is replacing human judgment, and so people who might have had the chance to develop practical judgment in these areas no longer will.
passages.zh: 在工作场所，管理者经常要决定雇用或解雇谁，以及批准哪笔贷款，等等。在这些领域，算法处方正在取代人的判断，因此，那些原本可能有机会在这些领域培养实践判断力的人，将不再拥有这样的机会。

passages.en: Recommendation engines, which are increasingly prevalent intermediaries in people's consumption of culture, may serve to constrain choice and minimize luck. By presenting consumers with algorithmically selected choices of what to watch, read, stream and visit next, companies are replacing human taste with machine taste. In one sense, this is helpful. After all, machines can survey a wider range of choices than any individual is likely to have the time or energy to do on their own.
passages.zh: 推荐引擎日益成为人们文化消费中普遍存在的中介，它们可能会限制选择并减少偶然性。通过向消费者展示由算法选择的下一部要观看、阅读、通过流媒体收听或访问的内容，公司正在用机器品味取代人的品味。从某种意义上说，这很有帮助。毕竟，机器能够考察比任何个人都更广泛的选择，而个人很可能没有时间或精力独自完成这件事。

passages.en: At the same time, though, this selection is optimizing for what people are likely to prefer based on what they've preferred in the past. We think there is some risk that people's options will be constrained by their past in a new and unanticipated way.
passages.zh: 不过与此同时，这种选择是在根据人们过去的偏好，优化他们可能会喜欢的内容。我们认为，人们的选择可能会以一种全新且出乎意料的方式受到其过去经历的限制，这其中存在一定风险。

passages.en: As machine learning algorithms improve and as they train on more extensive data sets, larger parts of everyday life are likely to become utterly predictable. The predictions are going to get better and better, and they will ultimately make common experiences more efficient and pleasant.
passages.zh: 随着机器学习算法不断改进，并在更大规模的数据集上进行训练，日常生活中更大范围的部分很可能会变得完全可预测。预测将变得越来越准确，并最终使常见体验更加高效、愉快。

passages.en: Algorithms could soon—if they don't already—have a better idea about which show you'd like to watch next and which job candidate you should hire than you do. One day, humans may even find a way for machines to make these decisions without some of the biases that humans typically display.
passages.zh: 算法很快就可能，或者说如果现在还没有的话，能够比你自己更清楚地判断你下一步想看哪部节目，以及你应该录用哪位求职者。有一天，人类甚至可能找到一种方法，让机器在作出这些决定时避免人类通常表现出的某些偏见。

passages.en: But to the extent that unpredictability is part of how people understand themselves and part of what people like about themselves, humanity is in the process of losing something significant. As they become more and more predictable, the creatures inhabiting the increasingly AI-mediated world will become less and less like us.
passages.zh: 但是，如果不可预测性是人们认识自我的方式之一，也是人们喜欢自身特点的一部分，那么人类正在逐渐失去某种重要的东西。随着这些生物变得越来越可预测，生活在这个日益由人工智能中介的世界中的生物，将越来越不像我们。

questions.stem: What do we learn about the deeper implications of AI?
questions.stem_zh: 关于人工智能更深层次的影响,我们了解到什么?

options.text: It is causing catastrophic levels of unemployment.
options.zh: 它正在造成灾难性的失业水平。

options.text: It is doing physical harm to human operators.
options.zh: 它正在对人类操作者造成身体伤害。

options.text: It is altering moral judgments.
options.zh: 它正在改变道德判断。

options.text: It is reshaping humanity.
options.zh: 它正在重塑人类。

questions.判型: 题干What do we learn about the deeper implications of AI?是直接问对某概念了解到的内容，没有infer/imply等推断信号。
questions.拆句: Q46是一个标准的what引导的特殊疑问句，主干是"What do we learn about X"，about后接the deeper implications of AI整个名词短语，无陷阱。
